references.text: Earlier (in [ref:Luk 22:16|Luke 22:16]) Jesus says something similar about the Passover meal – that he will not eat it until it is fulfilled in God's kingdom. Both statements point toward the eschatological fulfillment.

In [ref:Matt 26:29|Matthew 26:29] Jesus says at the Last Supper: "I will not drink again of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom." This is a parallel to Luke's version of the same statement.

In [ref:Mark 14:25|Mark 14:25] Jesus says: "Truly, I say to you, I will never again drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in God's kingdom." This is Mark's parallel account of the same promise.

In [ref:Apg 1:3|Acts 1:3] it is told that after his resurrection Jesus appeared to the disciples over a period of forty days and spoke about matters concerning the kingdom of God, which connects to Jesus' promise about the coming of God's kingdom.

In [ref:Åp 19:6-9|Revelation 19:6–9] the marriage supper of the Lamb is described, where believers are invited to the eschatological feast. Jesus' words about drinking wine again when God's kingdom comes point toward this final joy of celebration.

In [ref:Jes 25:6-9|Isaiah 25:6–9] Isaiah prophesies about the great feast the Lord will hold for all peoples on Mount Zion – with wine and rich dishes. Jesus' promise to drink wine in God's kingdom reflects this Old Testament expectation of the messianic feast.

In [ref:Luk 13:29|Luke 13:29] Jesus speaks of people coming from east and west to sit at the table in God's kingdom. The eschatological meal that Jesus looks forward to here is the same as he refers to in 22:18.

In [ref:Luk 14:15|Luke 14:15] one of the guests says: "Blessed is the one who will eat at the feast in God's kingdom!" This statement confirms the expectation of a future meal in God's kingdom, which Jesus refers to in his promise to drink wine again.
